bio: Cyril and Methodius were brothers from Thessaloniki. In 863 they created the Glagolitic alphabet, the first written script for the Slavic language, and translated the scriptures into it. Their disciples, Clement and Naum of Ohrid among them, carried their work on, and the Cyrillic alphabet used in Macedonia today grew out of it. The university in Skopje is named after them.
